title: Domain VI: Contract Development & Administration - Contract Development & Administration - Supplier Compliance
subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In a managed services contract, the vendor agrees to maintain 99.9% network uptime. This specific measurable commitment is outlined in the:
questions.explain: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) defines the specific level of service expected from a vendor, laying out metrics (like uptime) and penalties/remedies if targets are missed.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: To systematically measure vendor performance against the contract requirements over time, a contract manager tracks quantifiable metrics known as:
questions.explain: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are specific, quantifiable measurements used to track a vendor's performance and ensure compliance with the contract's objectives.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: When a vendor fails to perform a critical contract requirement, what formal document is typically sent to notify them of the deficiency and give them a defined number of days to fix the issue before termination?
questions.explain: A Cure Notice formally informs the contractor of their default and grants them a specified timeframe (often 10 days) to 'cure' or fix the deficiency before the agency terminates for default.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a vendor fails to resolve a performance issue after the timeframe specified in a Cure Notice has expired, what is the most appropriate next step for the contracting officer?
options: Issue a Show Cause Notice or a Termination for Default.
Issue a second Cure Notice extending the timeframe indefinitely.
Approve full payment and assign the work to an internal department.
Renegotiate the contract to lower the required standards.
questions.explain: If the cure period lapses without resolution, the agency typically escalates by issuing a Show Cause Notice (asking why they shouldn't be terminated) or immediately issues a Termination for Default.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of issuing a 'Show Cause Notice' to a non-compliant vendor?
options: To provide instructions on how to submit their final invoice.
To demand the vendor stop all work immediately.
To afford the vendor a final opportunity to present reasons why the contract should not be terminated for default.
To officially invoke the termination for convenience clause.
questions.explain: A Show Cause Notice is used when default is imminent. It demands that the contractor 'show cause' or explain why they should not be held liable and why the contract should not be terminated.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A contractor misses a critical construction deadline, triggering an assessment of $1,000 per day in Liquidated Damages. From a contract administration perspective, what is the nature of this assessment?
options: It is a punitive fine designed to punish the vendor.
It is a pre-estimated contractual remedy to compensate the agency for losses caused by the delay.
It is an illegal deduction under public procurement law.
It replaces the need for standard invoice processing.
questions.explain: Liquidated damages are an agreed-upon mechanism representing a reasonable pre-estimate of the agency's actual damages incurred due to the vendor's delay, not a penalty.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A vendor delivers a software module that meets 95% of the specifications but contains minor bugs that do not hinder its primary operational function. In contract law, this vendor has achieved:
questions.explain: Substantial performance occurs when a contractor fulfills the essential purpose of the contract, even though slight, minor omissions or defects exist. The agency cannot terminate for default but may seek a price reduction.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A janitorial contractor fails a monthly inspection. The contract manager requires the contractor to submit a document outlining how they will fix the current issue and prevent it from recurring. This document is a:
questions.explain: A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) is developed by the vendor in response to performance deficiencies, detailing the root cause of the problem, the solution, and steps to prevent future occurrences.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: When administering a complex service contract (like facility maintenance), the agency relies on a document that dictates exactly how, when, and what it will evaluate to ensure contractor performance. This document is the:
questions.explain: The QASP serves as the government's roadmap for contract monitoring, establishing the methods, schedule, and criteria for inspecting and evaluating vendor performance.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: For low-cost, high-volume commodity orders (e.g., millions of pens), which inspection strategy is the most cost-effective for ensuring compliance while minimizing agency labor?
questions.explain: Random sampling (or statistical sampling) is used for high-volume, low-risk items where checking every single item (100% inspection) is financially or logistically impractical.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A construction contract allows the agency to hold back 5% of each progress payment until final project completion. This mechanism, used to ensure final compliance and leverage against defects, is known as:
questions.explain: Retainage is a portion of the agreed-upon contract price deliberately withheld until the work is substantially complete to assure that the contractor will satisfy their obligations.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: During documentation of poor supplier performance, which characteristic is essential for the documentation to be legally defensible in a dispute?
options: It must contain emotional appeals to vendor loyalty.
It must be completely subjective based on end-user opinions.
It must be objective, factual, clearly tied to contract requirements, and well-dated.
It must not be shared with the vendor to maintain the element of surprise.
questions.explain: Objective, fact-based documentation that directly references the breached contract terms is vital for supporting adverse actions like payment deductions or termination.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A vendor chronically delivers goods three days late. For six months, the agency accepts the late goods without complaint or penalty. When the agency finally tries to terminate for default based on late delivery, the vendor could successfully argue:
questions.explain: By repeatedly accepting late deliveries without enforcing the contract's delivery schedule, the agency inadvertently 'waived' its right to strict enforcement through estoppel, establishing a new accepted pattern of performance.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In a Prime Contractor/Subcontractor relationship, if the subcontractor fails to deliver on time, causing the prime to miss the deadline, who is legally responsible for the default to the purchasing agency?
questions.explain: Privity of contract exists only between the agency and the Prime Contractor. The Prime is fully responsible for the performance and compliance of its chosen subcontractors.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: To ensure transparency and compliance with billing rates on a Time and Materials contract, which contract clause must the agency include and actively exercise?
questions.explain: A Right to Audit clause grants the purchasing agency the authority to review the contractor's financial records, timesheets, and invoices to verify that the amounts billed are accurate and compliant.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A supplier voluntarily informs the contract administrator, 'Due to supply chain failure, we will not be able to fulfill the delivery required next month.' Under the UCC, this premature declaration of default is known as:
questions.explain: Anticipatory repudiation occurs when one party to a contract unambiguously indicates, before performance is due, that they will not fulfill their contractual obligations.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: When assessing performance, standard commercial items (like standard office paper) come with a built-in unwritten promise that they are reasonably fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used. This is called the:
options: Implied Warranty of Fitness for a Particular Purpose
questions.explain: Under the UCC, the implied warranty of merchantability guarantees that a product sold by a merchant is basic, functional, and suitable for the ordinary purpose for which it is intended.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a buyer explicitly relies on the vendor's specialized expertise to select the exact right software for a very specific, unique agency need, and the software fails to meet that need, the vendor likely breached the:
options: Implied Warranty of Fitness for a Particular Purpose
questions.explain: This implied warranty is created when a seller knows the specific purpose for which goods are required and the buyer relies on the seller's skill to select suitable goods.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In compliance monitoring, what is an 'Incentive Contract' designed to achieve?
options: To penalize vendors who miss minimum delivery dates.
To align the contractor’s financial interests with those of the agency by offering additional profit for exceeding specific cost, schedule, or performance targets.
To convert a firm-fixed-price contract into a time-and-materials contract.
To ensure the lowest responsive bidder receives the initial award.
questions.explain: Incentive contracts are structured to motivate the contractor to perform better, faster, or cheaper by tying their profit/fee directly to their performance against predetermined targets.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: During formal vendor performance evaluations (e.g., vendor report cards), when should performance expectations ideally be set to ensure fair compliance scoring?
options: At the conclusion of the contract right before final payment.
During the pre-solicitation and solicitation drafting phases, and reiterated at the post-award meeting.
Immediately after the first failure occurs.
When an auditor requests the file.
questions.explain: To fairly evaluate a vendor, performance metrics and expectations must be clearly defined in the initial solicitation/contract documents and confirmed early at the post-award meeting.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a contract administrator observes a safety violation on a construction site that represents an imminent threat to human life, what is their immediate compliance authority?
options: Send a written Cure Notice giving 10 days to resolve the safety hazard.
Issue an immediate verbal or written Stop Work order for the affected area until the hazard is mitigated.
Deduct $500 from the next progress payment.
Wait until the next scheduled quarterly performance review to bring it up.
questions.explain: When imminent danger to life, health, or property exists, the contract administrator has the authority and responsibility to issue an immediate stop-work order to mitigate the risk.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A contractor claims they cannot perform due to a global pandemic and supply chain collapse. This is considered an 'Excusable Delay'. What is the practical result for the contractor regarding compliance?
options: They are granted additional time to perform without being subject to default terminations or liquidated damages.
They are entitled to double payment due to the hardship.
They are automatically terminated for convenience.
They must secure a new performance bond within 24 hours.
questions.explain: An excusable delay (Force Majeure) relieves the contractor from liability (e.g., liquidated damages or default) because the failure to perform is beyond their control and without their fault or negligence.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A vendor submits a progress report indicating they are 50% complete, but the agency's QA inspector verifies they have only completed 20% of the work. What financial control prevents overpayment?
options: Performance bonds only pay out at 100% completion.
The agency cross-verifies milestones via the Receiving Report/QA inspection before approving progress payments.
The agency cannot prevent overpayment but can sue later.
The vendor is protected under the prompt payment act.
questions.explain: Progress payments must be directly tied to verifiable progress. The agency inspector's verification serves as the internal control (receiving report equivalent) that prevents paying for work not yet performed.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Material Breach and a Minor Breach of contract?
options: A Minor Breach completely excuses the non-breaching party from further performance.
A Material Breach severely impairs the core value or purpose of the contract, giving the agency the right to terminate.
A Minor Breach must be cured within 30 days, while a Material Breach requires 60 days.
Only Minor Breaches allow the agency to claim actual damages.
questions.explain: A material breach strikes at the heart of the contract, defeating its purpose and allowing the injured party to terminate the contract. A minor breach requires the parties to continue performance but allows for damage recovery.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A compliance matrix (or Requirements Traceability Matrix) is often used during active execution. What is its main administrative function?
options: To cross-reference and track each specific contract requirement against the vendor's ongoing deliverables and test results.
To calculate the final retainage percentage.
To map out the vendor's internal organizational chart.
To list the environmental laws of the state.
questions.explain: A compliance or requirements matrix ensures nothing is missed by tracing each specific contract requirement from the statement of work to the vendor's deliverables and validation tests.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration
